data.title: Validate and stabilize data mapping prerequisites
data.when: When running any complex data transformation, mapping, or configuration amendment that fails mysteriously in a local or cheaper development environment, but succeeds when tested in a stronger CI or dedicated staging tier.
procedure: Review the specific error message to identify which external assumption or 'expectation' is failing (e.g., required environment variable missing, dependency version mismatch, prerequisite data state not yet established).
Explicitly implement a preliminary validation step at the start of the task flow dedicated solely to setting and confirming all necessary expectations and prerequisites for the mapping logic.

Use logging or assertion statements to confirm that all dependencies (data models, external services, configuration values) are present and in the expected state before proceeding with the core 'amendment' logic.
Test this prerequisite validation step independently to ensure it fails fast if any expectation is violated, thus preventing resource escalation.
pitfalls: Treating the symptom (adding a check) instead of the cause (an underlying dependency that needs version alignment or architectural review).
Making the skill too brittle by hardcoding values; the validation must be dynamic and environment-aware.
The fix itself becoming another point of failure if the scope of the missing expectation is wider than initially identified.
verification: The mapping task runs successfully end-to-end on the cheaper tier without manual intervention or requirement for escalating resources/environments.
Running the validation step (the preliminary checks) explicitly confirms all required expectations are met, producing clear logs of success or failure.
